decisive_step: The 'real inflation adjusted silver price at that time' for Sept 1938/1948/1958 does not exist anywhere in the corpus (reference worklog steps 12-14 and review.md section 4 searched the 1930s-1960s issues; solution.structured.json lists the prices as EXTERNAL KNOWLEDGE recalled from memory; the exact statutory rate is also absent, only a rounded 'per fine ounce' figure appears in the column header, worklog steps 15-16). The reference used its recalled market prices and was graded wrong, and the wording is internally inconsistent (worklog Parse, ambiguity 1), so no cell could reach the key from the corpus. The in-corpus part is settled and every cell got it: total silver monetary stock at the statutory value from 'Monetary Stocks of Gold and Silver' (treasury_bulletin_1939_01.txt:1447, 1948_12.txt:2849 revised from the preliminary 1948_11.txt:2764, 1958_11.txt:3478), with the Components table's total column agreeing (1939_01.txt:1481, 1948_12.txt:2913).

smallest_change.change: Hard loop breaker (operational, not a correctness fix): when the actor issues a command identical to one already run N=3 times with identical output, the harness does not execute it; it returns the first 20 lines of the cached output followed by one line '[harness:loop] not re-run: identical to call <k> (<n> repeats, output unchanged). Run a different command, or submit.' This changes what the model sees on every repeat, unlike the note-only guard whose 3-note cap left b silent for 294 repeats and which cell a (text-only) did not have at all. Cell a: 139 repeats, ~28 min, 23.7M input tokens; cell b: 297 repeats, ~47 min, 48M input tokens, one compaction and a transport retry; both ended on the same answer they could have submitted at a[62]/b[31].
smallest_change.could_hurt_right_cells: unlikely: it only intercepts an exact command whose output is already known to be identical; a deliberate re-run after a state change would differ in text or output

fix.why_not_text: The decisive input is absent from the corpus, so no sentence can supply it. For the operational failure: cell a had the 'Loops' sentence and the strongest loop of all cells; cell b had the loop-note control and still looped after its 3-note budget was spent. Only a control that alters the tool output on repeats changes the model's next step.
fix.irreducible: Yes for correctness. The key requires an external silver price series (and its 'real vs nominal' reading) that the corpus does not contain; the reference solution with recalled prices was graded wrong, and the four cells split between 'skip the price' (a, b, b2: identical answer) and 'recall a CPI-adjusted price' (c). v8 none/prompt/cards were also all wrong. Nothing an adapter controls can reach the key here; the question should be excluded from adapter scoring or flagged like an issue47 case.

notes: (1) This question is a cost sink, not a signal: a+b together spent ~75 min and ~72M input tokens to submit the same value b2 reached in 24 min and a could have reached at a[62]. The v10 loop control should intercept, not annotate. (2) The printings header-parse defect on the 1939 Components table is real and reproducible: the multi-level header 'Total silver at ... per ounce' is attached to the subsidiary-coin column (c7) in 7 of 10 issues and to the true total (c8) in 3; the SUMMARY then calls the true total the outlier. The same pattern appears in 1958-59 issues (b2[23]: two 'total' columns, one flagged ISOLATED). A column-index-consistency warning (alternative 1) would have changed what a, b2 and c saw. (3) Post-compaction ledger splice in b listed the most recently touched cells, which were an unrelated import-quota table, so the splice carried nothing about the question; 'latest first' is the wrong ordering when the tail of a long run is noise. (4) c probed config.toml and .harness (c[79]-[80], c[90]) looking for hidden data; harmless here but worth a README line. (5) The v8 per-question file referenced in index.json (per-question/010.json) is absent from the folder.
